phases.title: Program
phases.intent: Coordinate the complete Browser-WASM program and keep product claims tied to completed evidence.

phases.title: Architecture and decisions
phases.intent: Freeze boundaries before implementation so the program does not drift into a full port of native q-runtime or a JavaScript-only mock.

phases.title: Portable Rust/WASM kernel
phases.intent: Put compatibility-critical, host-independent semantics on the real Rust/WASM request path.

phases.title: Browser runtime and Worker execution
phases.intent: Provide a real browser runtime over Request/Response, isolated handler execution, and Treaty without a listening application server.

phases.title: Compiler, artifacts, and static deployment
phases.intent: Turn the runtime into deterministic static artifacts that can be built, inspected, updated, rolled back, and hosted generically.

phases.title: Browser capabilities and persistence
phases.intent: Expose only browser-safe capabilities, support explicit local persistence, and fail closed for production-only requirements.

phases.title: Conformance, security, DevEx, and release qualification
phases.intent: Prove cross-target semantics, browser support, security, performance, documentation, and clean external usability.

phases.title: Optional QuickJS-NG WASM parity
phases.intent: Investigate closer QuickJS-NG engine parity without silently making it a prerequisite for the practical MVP.

phases.title: Release gate
phases.intent: Review one exact candidate and make an unambiguous GO or NO-GO decision.
